definition: A standardized document accompanying a released model that describes its intended uses, limitations, training data, and evaluation results.
details: Model cards promote transparency by giving downstream users and developers the information needed to assess whether a model is appropriate and safe for their intended use case.

explainer.lead: A standardized document released with a model that states its intended uses, limitations, training data, and evaluation results. It matters for transparency: downstream users get the information needed to judge whether a model is appropriate and safe for their use case.

tiers.eli5: It is like a nutrition label on food, telling you what went into the model and what it should and should not be used for.
tiers.practitioner: Teams publish model cards alongside weights or APIs so consumers can assess fit before adopting. A pitfall is that a sparse or overly generic card gives false assurance rather than real transparency.
tiers.paperLevel: A standardized accompanying document covering intended uses, limitations, training data, and evaluation results; its value is bounded by the honesty and specificity of those reported fields.

explainer.example: A released model ships with a card listing its evaluation results, known limitations, and the uses it is not intended for.
